newsitem.title: USA: DC council clears sale of $45 mln in museum bonds.
newsitem.headline: DC council clears sale of $45 mln in museum bonds.

text.p: The District of Columbia Council on Tuesday approved the sale of $45 million in revenue bonds to remodel a popular museum in the Smithsonian Institution complex, a city official said.

Michael Hodge, D.C. assistant treasurer and manager of the city's industrial revenue bond program, said the sale will represent the first time a federal museum installation has been financed with tax-exempt bonds.
Bond proceeds will be used to expand or construct additions to the west court of the National Museum of Natural History, Hodge said.
The Smithsonian will build a new 488-seat, 3-D IMAX theater for developing educational films and a state-of-the-art "interactive" facility to educate visitors about ecology, the city said.
Proceeds also will go to expanding the museum's restaurant and shop, the city said.
The District is expected to name an underwriter this week on the deal.

D.C.'s council also approved sale of another $45 million in revenue bonds to allow the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Center for Education and Medicine Inc. to refund $36.6 million in bonds issued in 1990, Hodge said.
